ai.description: This stout, globular frog reaches 7.5 cm. It is brownish-yellow with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a pale belly. Key features include a small, pointed head and shovel-like metatarsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Uperodon taprobanicus* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow or orange spots scattered across its dark, brownish-grey dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: The Sri Lankan Bullfrog inhabits lowland moist forests, scrublands, and agricultural areas, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Sri Lankan Bullfrog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground to retain moisture before emerging to hunt insects after rain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon taprobanicus* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of up to 2,000 eggs in temporary rain pools, where they undergo rapid larval development.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sri Lankan Bullfrog occurs across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Deccan Plateau and coastal plains from sea level up to 1,000 meters elevation.
ai.callDescription: The Sri Lankan Bullfrog produces a loud, low-pitched, repetitive "wook-wook" call, typically heard emanating from flooded fields and temporary pools during the monsoon.
